newsitem.title: USA: N.J. says fiscal 1997 revenues total $13.1 bln.
newsitem.headline: N.J. says fiscal 1997 revenues total $13.1 bln.

text.p: New Jersey collected $13.1 billion in revenues for the first 10 months of fiscal 1997, exceeding projections by 1.3 percent, state Treasurer Brian Clymer said Tuesday.
Clymer said collections were "especially strong" for the month of April, with $2 billion of revenues hitting state coffers, or 7.8 percent more than forecasts predicted.

For the 10 months ended April 30, Clymer said gross income tax and corporation business tax revenues "significantly outpaced expectations," while lottery, motor vehicle fees, and transfer inheritance taxes trailed projections.
Sales tax revenues are on target, he said.

The income tax generated more than $4.1 billion for the period, $100 million above forecasts, and corporate business taxes totaled more than $1.1 billion, 13 percent higher than revised expectations. Lottery collections were $522 million, or $15.8 million below projections.
Clymer is scheduled on Wednesday to discuss the state's revenue outlook before the Joint Legislative Appropriations Committee.
Several state lawmakers have said they would use the strong revenue figures to argue against the need for Gov. Christine Whitman's plan to borrow $2.8 billion to pay off unfunded pension liabilities.
